title: Excruciatingly inefficient
text:
I have to say that both the service and the app are incredibly inefficient. My recent experience is illustrative. A simple request required a more than three hour phone call, speaking with five different staff members and waiting on numerous holds.  This was followed up by messages in the app requesting information already provided, with exceptional delays, including requiring me to update the software, repeatedly fill out the same unnecessary questionnaire, repeatedly provide personal contact information already there, multiple requests to recreate the backup pin number, and repeated requirements to login again.  My time is valuable, and this process is unduly burdensome for anyone, let alone patients fresh out of surgery. It is simply unacceptable.  Accolade should be paying me for my time. Do better. 

And a postscript: the musical sample that plays over and over again while on hold if you call Accolade has to have been selected to intentionally discourage callers from waiting on hold. The volume range and shrill notes are completely inappropriate.

title: Your insurance’s outsourced customer service
text: To be clear: Accolade is your insurance company’s outsourced customer service platform. They may hide behind the “care advocate” name, but they really are there to insulate insurance companies from customer complaints, frustrations, and to further gum-up the process of having claims approved and processed in a timely manner. And to be clear: they do a great job at this. The number of hours that I’ve spent trying to re-explain claim issues to each and everything new “advocate,” chasing down reimbursements, and pleading with Accolade to help me receive care under the terms of my plan only to be patronized with some lip service about how they work for us and not the insurance companies. If you’re working with Accolade be prepared to be your own advocate — and set aside a lot of free time for each need you have.

text:
I really enjoy the Alliant app and have been getting more comfortable with it as I learn my way around. Overall, I think it’s a great platform and I truly appreciate what you’ve built.

One feature I would love to see in the future is the ability to link directly with doctors or healthcare providers. I’m learning as I go, trying to stay in-network and manage things the right way, and having some level of integration or guidance there would be extremely helpful.

The only real challenge I’ve run into is customer support response time. I currently have a case number open related to getting my phone number and bank account added, and I haven’t received a reply yet. It would be great if there were a more streamlined system or quicker acknowledgment—something as simple as a confirmation that the support team is actively working the request.

That said, I truly do love the app and the direction it’s going. Keep up the good work, and I’m excited to see how it continues to improve.

title: No longer a meditation app
text:
This app used to be phenomenal for building a real meditation practice back in 2018 or so. Since being bought out by $4B AI health tech company Sword Health, they’ve gutted the core focus on mindfulness and replaced it with a flood of 4-minute snippet personal affirmations.

Years ago, I used Headspace to learn legitimate techniques inspired by traditional buddhist monk training, extending my sits to 30 or 60 minutes with results that changed my life. Now, the app is jam-packed with "mood boosters," white noise, and audio clips for doing jumping jacks. The actual courses on how to meditate have either evaporated or been buried deep under layers of menus.

If you truly want to learn the practice of meditation, look elsewhere. If you want a 3.5-minute mini podcast telling you how to overcome imposter sydrome while the host reminds you to breathe, this app is for you.

[My understanding is this bite-sized content has been designed to pad engagement stats, which fatten Sword Health’s $4B valuation and prep the company for an IPO. as usual $$$ ruins everything]

I’ve been using Headspace to meditate for 8 years now and it’s something I keep coming back to. After trying other forms of mindfulness, as well as TM, this app seems to be the way that works to keep me practicing consistently. 

My only critique is that it doesn’t make it easy to continue doing previous meditations. Especially if you’re doing a course. Instead of saving the course to your history, you have to go in and manually find the course every time you want to continue. This can be especially annoying because sometimes courses have similar names or subject matter. Also, you aren’t always able to save a meditation to your “favorites”, making some hard to find when you want to revisit them.

Still love it, but would appreciate a more accessible format more than I need extra features like workout videos.

title: Headspace
text:
Based on my own experience of the Headspace app, I would give the product 4 out of 5 stars. My experience was largely positive, with specific strengths being ease of navigation, visual appeal, relevant and helpful material, accessibility options, and a wide range of content. This praise does not come without concerns, however, although some of the concerns may not directly come to mind as an adolescent. I worry about some of the privacy collection aspects of Headspace, although I am unsure how relevant this would be to the 13 year old looking for help with coping strategies. There are some concerns from an adolescent point of view, namely how little engagement there is in each activity. There are also limited opportunities for peer connection and a pretty hefty price tag starting in 2027.
Adolescence is a major point of change in a human’s life. Similarly to early childhood, there is a heightened point of brain plasticity that allows for the brain to change and adapt to new experiences. There was a time where individuals viewed this period of a child’s life as simply something that you just needed to get to the other side of. Laurence Steinberg challenges this idea and sees adolescence as an opportunity for children to truly develop certain skills. In his interview with Jonathan Singer on The Social Work Podcast, Steinberg (2018) states that this time is crucial for developing non-cognitive skills like mindfulness and mediation for self control. Headspace crucially allows space to develop these skills. If I am a student who is having trouble with transitioning to a new school or grade and looking for concrete ways to find relief, I have an app at my fingertips that will carefully guide me through exercises that teach me lasting coping skills. Lessons have colorful animations that engage me and durations that can be as short as 2 minutes if I am in a rush. 
In his book The Age of Opportunity, Steinberg also mentions how adolescence is beginning earlier and ending later. Steinberg (2014) states “a longer period between the start of adolescence (when the brain becomes more easily aroused) and when it ends (when brain systems that govern self-regulation have finally matured) means a longer period of imbalance, and greater exposure to all sorts of problems” (15). Headspace provides free plans for individuals as young as 13, meaning they can take advantage of this period of neuroplasticity to build healthy habits. This is a tool they could carry with them through this extended period of development, as the extensive library provides content all the way through later adolescence and into adulthood. The sooner children can find ways to cope with this greater exposure to problems, the better off they can be for future stages of development.
Adolescence is a time of increased autonomy. In Working with adolescents: A guide for practitioners, Laser & Nicotera (2021) note that “the youth moves from the external control of childhood moral behavior to autonomy and internal control in adolescence” (20). Adolescents increasingly want to have more control over their own lives and make their own decisions. Headspace gives them this opportunity to regulate their own behavior and emotions by allowing them to personalize their experience. They can open and use the app at their leisure and select which goals they want to work towards, which voices they want to hear, and how long they want to practice. An adult might recommend using the app, but this is an experience they get to maneuver on their own. Adolescents can eventually work towards independently recognizing when they need assistance and what they can do to help manage it. This is especially relevant because adolescence is the time where individuals experience more complex demands. Peer relationships become more important, identities begin to develop, there are increased academic demands, and family relationships may be changing as an adolescent works towards independence.
One large concern regarding Headspace comes from how adolescents view rewards. Laser & Nicotera (2021) explain that during adolescence, “the social-emotional brain, the limbic system, undergoes a change at about the time of puberty, 12–14 years old, which alters the youth’s attentiveness to rewards, sensation seeking, emotional arousal, short-term gratification, and adherence to social norms” (16). Headspace does not feed off of rewards in ways that might capture an adolescent’s attention directly. Of course, there is the reward of calming down from a stressful moment using one of the app’s exercises, but there is no instant sense of gratification for other parts of the app. There is a tracking feature that shows how many minutes and lessons have been experienced, and I believe that aspect could be expanded upon to increase engagement from adolescents. In the future, they may be able to include an awards page or allow for increased cosmetic profile customization as you progress through lessons.
Another drawback is how individual Headspace’s exercises are. Although you can share short segments of exercises with your friends, there is no way to directly connect with other individuals. Adolescence is a time where relationships and peer acceptance become increasingly important. These exercises can be helpful in some regards, as mindfulness can allow an adolescent to recognize when they feel socially overwhelmed and manage anxiety before entering a social situation, but there are no concrete ways to practice communication or develop relationships. Ultimately, these drawbacks are not significant enough to take away from the massive benefits this app provides for adolescents.

title: Lost their way a bit
text:
I have used Headspace off and on for many years. I really like the meditation techniques and courses that are on offer. The decidedly “non-mystical” approach to various techniques is very approachable and I can say that Andy, through is app, has taught me how to meditate. 

That said, I find myself quite bothered by all the noise that has been added to the app in recent years. From a “check in” message that seems to show up after every meditation, to themed daily messages, “social” threads on meditations (thankfully you can toggle these off), and ads for their newer therapy services, I find myself wishing for a simpler version of the app that no longer exists. 

None of these little “noisy things” are inherently problematic, I just don’t have need for them or interest in using them. The compounding effect (to me) is an app that feels like it’s trying really hard to get me to “engage” with it in a “deeper” way, when all I really want is simplicity and meditation exercises that I can come back to.

I’m tired of seeing little “try this” or “check this out”-type messages in the app every time I use it. I don’t want ads for therapy services, I don’t want to talk to an AI chatbot about my feelings. I don’t care about “relevant seasonal content” that helps me “cope with the pressures of existential dread” or whatever. I want a meditation app with useful exercises and techniques. 

To be clear, those other things aren’t necessarily bad things, and others may disagree with me, but all this makes me feel like Headspace doesn’t have an identity anymore. It’s devolving into another “content” app that’s vaguely focused on mental health or something like that, and is really just trying to make the most broadly useable app for the largest possible audience, for the largest possible number of subscribers. Just my opinion though.

title: Ebb is impressive
text:
I’ve been someone who has struggled with anxiety my whole life, and the mix of meditation and therapy this app provides has been really effective for me. I have a three-pronged system in place. I speak to my therapist twice a week, meditate once a day, and externalize to Ebb during flare-ups of anxiety. These three things working together has made me feel a sense of progress I haven’t felt in a long time.

Ebb has especially come a long way since I first tried to use it when it was first introduced. It asks good questions, makes interesting connections from prior conversations, and can make effective suggestions to navigate specific moments. This will never replace my therapy, but to have a place to catch anxiety in the moment, talk through the lessons I’ve learned from my therapy, and work through things quickly with a cognitive behavioral approach, helps me catch anxiety before my day begins to spiral.

Very impressed and curious to see where things go from here.

title: 10-year review
text:
i’ve had headspace for over a decade. for the first 3-4 years, I loved it. this app’s approach toward meditation and wellness has noticeably shifted since its inception though. When I started, it was Andy Puddicombe doing all of the meditations, translating what he learned as a monk into meditations everyday people could use and understand. he made those meditations accessible. I appreciated and learned from his approach towards meditation and life. eventually, Eve, Kessonga, and Dora joined, bringing a new lens that i really enjoyed too. they were different, but it still felt like their approach overlapped with andy’s, and I felt they complemented each other very well. these teachers taught me so much.

andy left a few years ago. the app has shifted in the years since—and many may like the new version! I honestly don’t know. But a couple of the new meditation teachers (not all of the new ones) make meditations and wellness exercises that don’t feel like they are teaching me anything new. They often feel closer to generic wellness content from an instagram influencer than a guided meditation. Some of the lessons they teach directly conflict with the lessons of the earlier generation of teachers. I chose headspace originally to be taught a form of meditation environment I could only easily find here. I want new teachers to have spent years studying, practicing, and guiding clients through that form of meditation. I also want them to align with apps original approach. 

And I know this shouldn’t matter to me, but I find it grating that one of the new teachers uses their platform to sell supplements. 

Anyway, it makes me feel sad to see how the perspective of headspace has changed. it’s trying to be so much. why is it offering therapy now? and AI diary entries? i miss when it was simpler app with diverse perspective unified by a common approach. but I still use headspace, because all of the earlier content is still available, and I have more to learn from it. And so that is what keeps me coming back and paying. But only because I haven’t found a suitable alternative yet. And that’s disappointing because ideally, I’d like my subscription to include new content in the style of the original meditations. 

p.s. Also, the app suddenly doesn’t work with my VPN which is dumb. why does my meditation app need to know my ip address? please fix the vpn issue.

title: AI isn’t a substitute for Human Care
text:
AI isn’t and never will be a replacement, or even a valid form of support, for mental health, no matter how it is framed. This is particularly true of AI chatbots like Ebb. There is no compassion, understanding, or genuine identification with another human being. Think of a TV set used as a babysitter.

I’ve been a Headspace subscriber for nine years, which makes the recent changes especially difficult to watch. The meaningful 30-day courses are largely gone, aside from a few exceptions. The menus are confusing and cluttered, with too many offerings lost in a “more is more” approach that dilutes what once felt thoughtful and intentional.

The introduction of streaks and numerical tracking has also been counterproductive for me. Instead of creating a sense of accomplishment, it adds pressure and stress. Turning a wellness practice into something you “win” by maintaining a number feels fundamentally misaligned with the purpose of mindfulness, which should be about care and presence, not badges or scores.

I use AI all the time. I am literally using it now to help polish this text. I’m not a caveman. But I do not believe anyone should turn to an AI chatbot like Ebb to talk through something as profound as losing a spouse to cancer. We are human. Humans help each other. Humans care for each other.

I believe Headspace is losing sight of this in its push to become a more profitable endeavor. You are losing me a little more each day, and I genuinely grieve that.

title: Truly a life saver
text:
I’ve been using the Calm app for about six years, and it has truly become one of my go-to tools.

My struggle with anxiety and overthinking is real. There are times when my mind simply does not want to slow down, and Calm has consistently given me a place to reset, breathe, refocus, and find a little peace.

Whether I need help quieting my thoughts, relaxing, sleeping, or just taking a few intentional minutes for myself, I know I can open the app and find something that meets me where I am.

I recommend Calm all the time and have shared it with so many people over the years because I genuinely use it and believe in it. Six years later, I’m still here—and that says a lot.

If you struggle with anxiety, overthinking, stress, or simply need a tool that reminds you to slow down and be present, Calm is absolutely worth trying.

title: Long-time subscriber lost because support simply doesn’t exist
text:
I was a long-time paying subscriber, and I finally cancelled.

The app stopped working properly for me, leaving me unable to reliably use a service I was paying a premium subscription price for. I contacted support for help.

They responded more than a month later.

By then, I had already cancelled my subscription because I refuse to continue paying for an app I cannot use while waiting weeks for someone to acknowledge the problem.

Technical issues happen. That isn’t why I’m leaving this review. I’m leaving it because a company charging this much for a subscription should provide a reasonable level of support when its paying customers cannot access the product they purchased.

What is particularly disappointing is that I actually liked the service. I subscribed for a long time. I wasn’t looking for a reason to cancel—I wanted someone to help me continue using something I was already happily paying for.

Instead, they turned a loyal subscriber into a former customer.

If you’re considering subscribing, understand that the price gets you access to the app when it works. Based on my experience, it does not get you timely help when it doesn’t.

A month-plus response time isn’t customer support. It’s an autopsy of a customer relationship that already died waiting.

I was forced to create an appointment to get my EAP sessions started. I’m sure there were other options I could have taken to finally get a real person to help with connecting my EAP. But when you’re in the middle of trying to mentally keep yourself afloat, you don’t think straight. title: Unfair Billing Practices, Poor Customer Service, and Provider Quality
text:
Skip it. $600 later, after my provider put me on a medication that made me feel worse, she fired me and told me to go to an in person psychiatrist. Then, after I am positive I cancelled my future appointments, I received a $125 cancellation charge on my card for an appointment I was not notified I still had for the following day. 

Well I did go and see and that “in person” psychiatrist. And they told me the Talkspace provider (who was operating under a LCMHP license, not a psychiatrist like the app filtered her profile for) had given me false and dangerous information about SSRI/SSNI/Stimulant classes of medication. The provider I see now was very disturbed at the Talkspace provider’s lack of understanding or knowledge of ADHD, and how SSRI/SSNI can negatively affect patients with this diagnosis. They can show signs of increased aggression and anxiety on these meds. 

Regarding the Talkspace provider, when I told her I wasn’t sure that I felt right on the medicine she prescribed, she recommended for me to go up. When that caused me to feel worse and more aggressive, she exhibited gaslighting behavior about my experiences, and she abandoned me as a patient and told me to ween off of the medicine on my own. 

Then she charged me a cancellation fee for canceling in a 24 hours window for an apt I’m quite sure I already cancelled previously, and I can’t even get ahold of a customer service number to refute the charge. Oh by the way, she fired me as a patient, remember? This company is likely over billing tons of people this way. 

I am thankful the provider I see now is properly educated in medication management and mental health diagnoses, understands what over medicating is, and how dangerous it can be to put someone on the wrong class of medication. 

This service is creating dangerous situations by not properly vetting their providers. Do not use them. They will take your money, put you on the incorrect meds—then abandon you.

Before I get into personal experience, for the app itself, I haven’t had any technical issues like I have in the past with telehealth type services, sending messages and making appointments is extremely simple, all information is easy to find & I feel the app itself has just been working flawlessly for me. I do explain I don’t care for the live messaging option personally although i can see how it may be beneficial for some especially with less complex problems. Now for personal experience, I was nervous it’d be a complete waste but kept an open mind. my first session I chose to do live messaging and I felt that wasn’t helpful at all, truthfully. The feature is a good idea in theory but just proved impractical. So I chose to do live audio next time and the difference was truly night and day, I did stay with the same therapist I was matched with originally for the audio session because I wanted to give them a fair chance & I felt the messaging wasn’t that. I was so glad I made that call, I wound up with a very insightful, kind, thorough session that was truthfully better than a therapist I had seen in the past in person. I have quite a few complex issues and still feel after just a few sessions that progress is being made & there is interest from mine and my therapists end to try and find the root of my problems so that we can fully attack the issue. All this to say, give it a shot. Worst case, you don’t click with your first second or maybe even third match, but if you’re looking for a good telehealth type option for therapy Talkspace is definitely a good option & worth the chance.

The support system is fundamentally broken. I have followed up through every possible channel, yet the platform fails to follow its own administrative protocols:

• The Ticket Void: I have submitted multiple tickets regarding technical issues and provider care. They do not respond consistently or quickly enough to resolve anything, leaving tickets open for weeks. Even when the Clinical Quality Team promises a 3-day response for serious complaints, they regularly blow past their own deadlines with no real updates even after I have followed up multiple times.

• Unreachable Phone Support: I tried calling their support line twice in the morning—specifically to avoid a queue—an hour apart. Both times, I was kept on hold for exactly 12 minutes before an automated voice claimed they were "closed" and hung up on me during their stated business hours.

• Agonizingly Slow Chat: Live chat agents take 5 minutes to respond to every single message, turning basic questions into painfully long ordeals that result in no resolution. All they do is direct you back to creating a ticket. If you’ve already done so, they then promise that you’ll get a response within three days, which you won’t. 


2. Lack of Transparency-

Talkspace provides no patient reviews for their therapists, forcing you into a "trial and error" loop. If their providers are to be trusted, they should be transparent with patient feedback so users can find a proper fit without constant provider changes.


3. Failure of Clinical Neutrality-

My spouse and I entered our first joint session in total agreement on our goals since we are separated. This is a rare and positive alignment for a separated couple. Yet, rather than celebrating our common goals, the therapist completely abandoned clinical neutrality to push her own narrative.

She criticized our intentions from the very start and claimed meeting as a family unit with our children would "confuse" them, ignoring our consensus that this was for their benefit. I had to politely ask her three times to stop questioning our intentions and redirect her back to our goals before she finally complied. It was an unprofessional attempt to create conflict and dysfunction where none existed.


Final Note to Talkspace: 

I have already reached out via email and followed up through every possible channel regarding these issues, so do not respond with a generic request for me to contact you again.

I honestly don’t expect anything to come out of this review or my open tickets because you have continuously made empty promises to resolve these issues. This lack of timely action is only creating more problems for me personally. Ultimately, this platform is marketed as a way to help you feel heard and safe, yet it fails to achieve that even within its own internal processes. You are not providing a safe space when your support is unreachable and your clinical oversight is terrible or non-existent.

text: I never write reviews, but I feel compelled to share my experience. I started using Talkspace because I was going through a lot and wanted to talk things through with a professional. I chose them because they accepted insurance, and the cost seemed reasonable. I’ve always been skeptical about therapy, partly because of the stigma that it means you’re ‘messed up,’ but I decided to give it a try. Unfortunately, my first appointment didn’t go as planned—the therapist canceled on me. At the time, I took it as a sign that therapy wasn’t for me, especially since I was still debating whether this was the right choice. Then, the therapist canceled on me again, this time with no notice, on the day of the session. Not even an email. I decided to switch therapists and got matched with a nice lady. However, the issue was that she would only listen and never offer any feedback. I just felt like we were very different people, and I struggled to connect with her. It felt like she wasn’t qualified for the things I was telling her. In truth, I never found a therapist on this platform that I felt comfortable with, though I only tried two. But that incident really upset me, when I missed an appointment by a few minutes—I had forgotten to set an alarm. Even though I joined late and the therapist was still there, I was charged a significant late fee. This felt unfair, especially since my first therapists had canceled on me without notice, and Talkspace never acknowledged or compensated me for those cancellations. I even have proof of those instances, so I’m not just speaking off the cuff. As someone already skeptical about therapy, this experience made me feel like it wasn’t worth the effort, at least not with this service/app. The fact that they charged me a fee for being a couple of minutes late, while they let their own cancellations slide without accountability, felt hypocritical and disheartening. Ultimately, I stopped trying with Talkspace and went somewhere that was in person. Which is so much better.

title: Not actually helpful mostly
text:
(This review is about Talkspace overall, not only a technical review of the app.) You have to dig deep into the FAQs to find this, but Talkspace says they offer "gentle support" for people who are otherwise functional. Basically if you don't actually need help then they can help. The system is convenient, including making payments and having them bill insurance directly, but not all of their therapists make their calendars available so scheduling can be difficult at times if your therapist is one of those. Avoid the psychiatric option (which is from an LPRN if you need or want medication) and see someone in person if that is your need. For talk therapy though the service may work for you. Another thing not said up front or by any therapist is that they do not do any disability paperwork. Unfortunately I had multiple therapists who said they would do it, then dropped the ball and didn't, and no one knew about the actual Talkspace policy on that. If you truly need help, look elsewhere probably. 

I do not recommend using the message-only option for a live appointment. It should be good in theory, but in reality the therapist may record an audio reply instead of typing, which introduces huge delays and doesn't allow for any kind of conversational flow. They also may not tell you when your time is up and will simply stop responding. 

From a tech review perspective, the app itself is pretty good. I've used it on my phone to connect audio only and with video, both at home LAN and while out using mobile data, and I've used a browser to do the same on multiple computers. The messaging function works well to communicate between or during appointments.

title: Are you sure the providers are licensed therapists??
text:
Upon signing up, I completed a billion forms about my current mental state, yet, when time came for the meeting with my provider, the woman didn’t even know if this was my first session or my 10th.
She then asked me what brought me in, and I began telling her about my anxiety problems. She didn’t even listen to me fully, the woman interrupted me talking and started giving me the most generic, googleable information on anxiety like ‘when we are stressed out it’s not good’ and ‘we need to find a balance’. Since that point, she didn’t let me talk or ask me any questions at all, she just kept going on about nothing, repeating the same thing over and over again, and then attempted to end our 30 minute sessions 14 minutes in.
I only then got a chance to speak on the actual reason why I was there in the first place (which she probably should have known according to all the forms I’ve filled out before meeting with her): my eating disorder. 
At that point, it felt like I was inconvenient to her, talking about why I am trying therapy. 
After I had told her a little about how I felt and how things are going for me (think 4 minutes), again she started going in and on for another 10 minutes nonstop. In those 10 minutes, she encouraged my obsession over weight loss, saying I could continue this with it still being healthy (I am not overweight). 
My plan consists of 1 live session a month and unlimited messaging. 
The provider informed me that she will not be responding to my messages, unless I book a ‘live chat’ session with her, meaning in general I would receive help for only 30 minutes a month.

So overall, I spend 30 minutes with only 2 extremely quick opportunities to speak, was encouraged by my provider to continue with my unhealthy behaviors, and wasted my only monthly shot and trying therapy on something that made me feel worse after.

Carefully consider this platform and what it offers, as it’s not at all what it is advertised at.
Super disappointed :(

title: Try somewhere else that values your mental health!
text: I was a client of Talkspace for three years (2019-2022) until my therapist took me off platform for private sessions. I could no longer afford those private sessions and received a voucher from my job for Talkspace that included four video calls per month and unlimited messaging. I thought great, I’ll jump back on Talkspace, messaging has always been my preferred so it would be nice to have both. I redeemed my code from my employer six weeks ago. In that time, I’ve tried four therapists. The first made me uncomfortable because I couldn’t verify her information on sites like Psychology Today. The second was abrupt and a bit rude-and flat out told me she wouldn’t use messaging and preferred video. The third had a lovely intro message but then cancelled our ten minute intro video and became unresponsive-she practically asked me to switch providers, but I asked if she’d mind if we gave it a shot since I had clicked with that first message. She said yes, but then went an entire week without replying to my messages. The fourth was great, and we really clicked during the intro consult. She unfortunately had to cancel our first actual session due to illness, and then did not respond for several days despite me seeing the double check mark “message delivered” beneath my message. As much as I liked her during the intro, I was really over Talkspace at this point and cancelled the service entirely because wondering why NO THERAPISTS ARE REPLYING TO ME is leaving my mental health in a worse place than when I started six weeks ago. I am uncertain if the difference between Talkspace now and Talkspace a couple years ago is that I was paying back then versus my company paying for it now? But this is not okay to do to people who are asking for help and already struggling with mental health. You cannot set expectations of “your therapist will be on a video at this time” (illness and emergencies exempt here!) or “you will receive at least one THOUGHTFUL response from your therapist each day they work” and then not follow through—no matter who is paying for the plan. The fact that I was 0/4 with therapists tells me something has changed in the service, and not for the better. These people have made me feel like an inconvenience for expecting to receive the service that was being paid for—and for someone who is already struggling with mental health, having to negotiate those feelings over the therapists themselves just makes the process so much harder than it should EVER be. The icing on the cake was the app repeatedly sending me assessments and notifications to use my video sessions before they expired. I would have LOVED to use them—but the service itself made it impossible and continued to charge my company and rub the unused sessions in my face. Dont use this service if you value responsiveness and/or your mental health. The way some of these therapists treat patients is completely unacceptable.

title: Expensive way to feel bad about yourself
text:
If you feel like you're hanging onto the edge of a cliff, TalkSpace offers a wonderful service where, for the low price of $400 a month, they'll step on your fingers and finish you off.

When you first join, they match you with a therapist at random, with absolutely no screening or filters beyond male vs female. My first therapist was so aloof and unsympathetic that I might as well have been talking to an AI. (In fact, I'm 95% sure I was.) So my first $100 week was spent trying to get any response out of her more sophisticated than "how do you feel about that".

My second $100 week was spent switching to a new therapist. And between the lag time, disclosures, and preliminary questions, it did in fact take a full week to get the ball rolling. 

Unfortunately, just when we were ready to begin the actual work, the therapist suddenly took a week off for vacation. He knew about the vacation when he took me on, promised he would be more sympathetic than the last therapist, then bailed just as we were starting. So my third $100 week is his vacation time. 

Almost a full month and I've still gotten absolutely no help. This service is beyond bad, it's downright harmful. All it's done is reinforce the fact that I am so utterly alone that I can't even PAY someone to talk with me. 

My suggestion: save your money and treat yourself to a nice vacation. It'll make you feel a lot better than this garbage service.

     If you came here for the text option I would advise not even trying. Had 1 out of 5 that would respond and was recently told I would get 2 messages a day for 5 days. Even with my copay that came out to $5 a message from them. Save yourself the headache and find someone local. This will only increase your anxiety dealing with Talkspace. 
      Their refund process seems to be just a bad as I’ve been waiting on a response for two days and have yet to have anybody reach out to me. Hopefully they make it right, but based on every experience up until now and seems like they got me for $100 and I only got worse.

title: Never assigned a therapist
text: After waiting over a week for a therapist to be assigned, I reached out to support and they told me my access code expired. It expired because they took so long to not assign a therapist. Support was no help. I do not recommend this service.

title: Double Check your insurance!
text:
My wife and I both put in our insurance info and Talkspace said our insurance would cover the services and we would pay $0. Awesome we thought, that was a major barrier to seeking care removed.

Two weeks after the sessions we get an email
Saying we will be charged because insurance will cover $0. So now we have an unexpected $250 bill and will be looking for another provider again.

I’d rather they just tell you to check directly with your insurance provider so we could have been avoided or least been prepared for the situation. 

Can’t speak for the service itself, because we only had a one live and a few chat sessions. But now we’re not sure we can afford it so will be looking into options covered by our insurance.

title: Great App!
text: Did my first session and I’m going to just say I am very satisfied with how things went! I feel heard and will be using this app for a very long time.

title: Super buggy
text: First, I was being told I couldn't see my therapist anymore for no reason and customer support made no sense and then it turns out they just had a mishap on their end after all. Next I'm being logged out of my account and I can't reset my password because "something went wrong" according to the app. I'm missing a session right now as I write this. So annoying.

title: Works well and convenient…
text: Works well and makes scheduling and communication easy and convenient.

title: Most Frustrating App
text:
My insurance covers talk space and I thought it was going to be awesome. It’s has been the most disappointing and frustrating experience of any app I’ve ever used. I had one session then I was received a notice to verify my insurance. Each time you verify your insurance it opens a new “room” and you may or may not get the same therapist. Each time I contact customer service it takes a day to get a response. They say I’m getting the insurance notice’s because I have multiple rooms open, but the system opens a room every time I verify. I feel
like I’m a tech savvy person but this has stumped me. Talk Space does NOT help your mental wellbeing!!!!!!

title: Messages hang out in no man’s land
text: My messages sit undelivered over a few days and then batch deliver all in one day. My therapist works 6 days a week and is always online. When the app works, it works well, but like deliver my darn messages already.

title: Life saver
text: This app has been tremendous in assisting me with my therapy because I do not have time to schedule each week to meet with someone during the day or in the evening because my schedules constantly changing. The therapist I’m currently working with has far exceeded my expectations and I’m hoping to continue therapy with her for a while.

title: Bad therapists, no choices
text: I was really hopeful about this app. I truly was struggling with anxiety, but unfortunately I have a couple of problems with the app and my experience while on the app. I wanted to find a provider who I felt was a good match for me but it seemed like the selection was pretty limited. Just an idea, but it would be really awesome if there was a filter about somethings you are looking for in a counselor. Also the counselor I had was just really not a good fit. I had to keep telling her/reminding her to send me the coping skills, examples of how to set boundaries, etc. She was always at least a couple mins late to every session and would leave early. The next counselor I signed up for never confirmed my appointment. I was really hopeful but very disappointed in your app. I know that not every counselor will be a good fit, and no app is perfect, but I just wanted to let you guys know what my experience was. I really hope that my experience was a rare occurrence.

title: Frustrating
text: You can’t call them, they mostly have male providers even when you request women. There app is not user friendly and their customer service is trash. If I didn’t like both of my therapists so much, I would not use this app.

title: Don’t do it
text: I have insurance and it gives me full coverage with a $0 copay for therapy and psychiatrists. I downloaded this app so I could possibly get help sooner. I input my insurance information and it still tried to charge me $66 per week first without even letting me confirm the legitimacy of their so called psychiatrists. Never trust any service that wants you to pay upfront it’s most likely a scam. Also if you have insurance just call the back of your card to get a list of services that your covered for.

title: Disappointed
text: I never write reviews but felt the need to express my frustration. First appointment with therapist great, mind you this is my first time in therapy, second meeting she’s late and often talks about the other platforms she is working with as well. I’m sorry this is my time I want to ensure I got the appropriate time to review my problems. Third visit, just received a new mental health DX and I knots talking to another healthcare professional would help me answer some questions. 15 minutes go by nothing. No message from her at all. She explains the struggles she is going through, 100% support that and understand we all have a lot of carp going on but it just goes to show why people give up and feel lost because practices close, therapist leave or just don’t show. Very disappointed with the level of unprofessionalism and the lack of I’ll regard to not even checking in or send a message. Silence is the deadliest to a mind who is always constantly thinking and therefore you spin further down.

title: Love love love
text: Great therapy

title: Customer service is useless
text: I start off by saying that initially signing up for TalkSpace I encountered numerous issues, one of them was able to resolve the issue and connect me with a provider that I genuinely liked talking with but out of no where, my coverage of using TalkSpace was gone when I had initially put the information in. I have Cigna and have already talked with them and they had told me that I was covered for TalkSpace. When I brought up the issue with the customer support, they took more than 5 days to reply to my issue at hand and suggested the same solution that I had already tried and didn’t work. I have put in at least 3 tickets dealing with the same issue and the customer support person was the same and told me the same thing. This has been going on for about a month now and I am fed up with it. There is no other form of communication other than emailing them and that doesn’t work. They need a customer support line as this is absolutely ridiculous that I am not able to get a manager or anyone other than the same tech person to help me resolve this problem. Not to mention that I am not able to set up a video session with my provider as the system does not appear to connect me with my provider. If I could I would’ve given it less stars as the system and app do not match with the service being provided. These are people that are dealing with mental health issues and shouldn’t have to be stressed out over not being able to talk with their therapist as they are paying for a service provided. This is what the tech support sent me on multiple times even after I informed the person that the he’s solution did not work. Hi there, Thank you for your follow-up! My apologies for the repeated issues here. At this time, it does not look like your insurance information was connected to this account. To re-apply your coverage to your existing account please follow the steps below: 1. Log in to your account on the web. 2. Click on your username 3. Select "Check my coverage" Once you receive this survey and click "Get Started", enter in your employer. We will check your eligibility for Talkspace and walk you through the process of getting started through your coverage. If you have any trouble matching with your original provider I can assist with switching you over, but please be sure to select a therapist at the end of the process regardless to finish making your new room. Once you have made a new room that includes your coverage, let me know and we can proceed with closing the invalid room. Let me know if you have any questions or need any assistance with this process. At your service, Patrick Talkspace Support. Not to mention later on I was getting billed for “sessions” that never occurred that were only the text conversations with the therapist to schedule my next session and not a legitimate session with the therapist. I highly recommend taking your business elsewhere because you’ll only have more added stress and lose money from it.

title: Poor user interface.
text:
This app has a lot of flaws in the user experience design. It does not allow you to move backwards through questionnaires. The survey for looking for a therapist is so limited and you get locked into a provider without at least getting a handful of providers you can choose from. It also locks you into a single problem when I know a lot of people who are struggling most likely have many issues they want to address. In this app you are either stressed, grieving, or depressed. Developers should allow the user to move back and forth and re take surveys for a better customer experience. You should also be allowed to at least preview therapists before scheduling an appointment. That way you can select a provider who specializes in the different areas you need help with. 

Overall, seeking a therapist is already an overwhelming experience and this made an already difficult task more challenging. For anyone who needs urgent help, I recommend trying other apps.

title: Awful
text: My therapist is good, but the platform and app aren’t. There’s no way to get in touch with people on the backend. They push you into new “rooms” when you update information but fail to update it on existing appointments. So they’re canceled. You can’t get in touch with anyone to get it fixed. Their chat is nothing but a bot sending you in loops and their messages are just answered with generic articles. It’s absolutely infuriating. This app also regularly has issues with sound, you can’t see app messages if you’re in an appointment you have to hang up to check them, and it also freezes quite a bit. Also, if you’re in a session and someone calls your phone you have sound issues and sometimes have to disconnect and reconnect. If my therapist wasn’t great, I’d definitely not recommend this app to anyone.

title: Predatory commercial practices
text: Talkspace is a predatory commercial practice company. Will tell you that no payment is due 3 times then charge you a full $100+. Causes more mental harm than relief. Avoid

title: Don’t waste your time and money.
text: The poorest customer service you can imagine. There’s no number to actually speak to someone when you have an issue, and they don’t get back to you when you submit a request. They charge you for services never rendered and even when you pause your account they will charge you for another month’s worth of sessions. It’s a shame because I really liked my therapist, and I’m not upset with her for having work/life balance, but it’s unacceptable to charge me for therapy I’m not receiving. This whole ordeal has had a negative impact on my mental health.

title: This is a Scam
text: Please do not use this app. They do not have good therapist or providers. They charge you for your full 4 weeks monthly and refuse to refund you if you cancel your subscription because their providers do not put in the effort to actually help you. I went through 5 providers and all of them were not professional and did not seem to know what they were doing. Additionally the experience years of the providers are false. One of my providers had on her file experience of 12 years however when I asked her about it she let it slip that she had only 3 months experience. If you truly need help please go somewhere else. They will make you feel worse instead of helping you. Do not go here or use this help. BetterHelp is a much better option and they truly do help you. Talkspace only cares about money and not your mental health.

title: Money grab
text: I tried this for several months with a couple of different therapists and all I feel is poorer. The app is very buggy and poorly designed. There are VERY few therapists to choose from and most of them are in their first year of practice. Sessions are too short and the therapists seem like Uber drivers - just getting a fare. Don’t recommend.

title: I feel mislead
text: Both this app and my work told me I’m covered. Come to find out I’m not and had a $125 charge come through, with 2 more probably on the way. No warning, nothing. This has screwed up my life, don’t trust the app.

title: Ugh!!
text: I should have changed my provider but i tried to just have patience and be open minded. Im pouring my heart out to this therapist about my frustrations and depression and her response? You should go outside. Maam im literally on edge of ending my life because OUTSIDE is my source of misery but SUNLIGHT is the answer?! Im over it. Worst experience of my life. If anything happens to me i want everyone to know my therapist failed me.

title: Surprising how much left to work out
text:
I can’t blame the app for quality of therapists- I think it does a lot to make therapy available to people. And I’ve had good experiences personally. But it isn’t a very user friendly format throughout. Signing up isn’t always super intuitive- if you put in insurance and it looks like they find it (you get clear message if they don’t at all) you go through a questionnaire and then they ask you to subscribe if they think your insurance doesn’t cover the sessions. So if something processed wrong, and say you know you have coverage for $20 copay, you aren’t clear from that screen before you subscribe whether it’s going through that way or not- maybe you think you’ll get reimbursed or something else-but they didn’t find that coverage. My insurance is weird and I had to try it under a couple different companies to get the coverage to show, but it finally showed the copay. But then randomly after an app update, they decided my coverage expired (my insurance hadn’t changed) and emailed me early the morning of a session, and 8 minutes later emailed to cancel the session to avoid fees. 
There is still no actual customer support you can talk to immediately- though the chatbot gives the false impression you might be connected to someone. You have to submit a message and wait up to 3 days if an article doesn’t help. This doesn’t seem like a great set up for people dealing with depression and anxiety and other issues- to have things like the app suddenly cancel their appointment for an issue that could be sorted with a couple minutes of human contact but you don’t have anyone available to sort it.

title: I leaving this app feeling more alone than when I began
text: I hit a breaking point and realized I needed help; advice, tools, somewhere I could say the things I’ve never been able to say. I regret giving this a try. I thought I felt hopeless , alone and unimportant when I decided to reach out and try to get better, but this experience confirmed it. I got 7 weeks of messaging, and three weeks in now, I went theough 5 providers. #1-3 asked identical questions about my traima, and other emotional subjects. I answered these these things three seperate times, crying on my phone screen hopeful I would be treated as a human being. Each time, days would go by before I got a response, and the response never addressed anything i said, I don’t think they even read it. When I got to my fourth provider immediately asked her if she was busy and thought it might be more than 3 days between messages. She said “my case load is full. It seems like you know how to find a new therapist….” Man, I wanted help feeling BETTER. I did not need help feeling worse. This is what I get for trying, even the people that you pay to be there have more important things to do. They’ll ask you to spend time in your trauma, and they’ll leave you alone with it for days. I might have kept trying, hot there was only two provider options after that, and I really don’t think I could take one more person trained in mental health having an opportunity to crap on mine. With not one single helpful or supportive word, I just don’t know how these “professionals” can do this to people who are only here because they need them. Pleas, so yourself a favor and try anything else. Me, I’m never trying anything again. Therapy is scam and I’ll just be broken until it kills me. Thanks Talkspace, for stealing my last bit of hope. Just keep walking through the world full of knives on your own.

title: Great experience
text: Found the right fit for me. I feel heard and validated and finally have some hope.

title: Stay away (Charges without treatment)
text:
I use Talkspace for about half a week during which point I realize most of the providers were completely unresponsive. One provider responded to me by telling me that she doesn’t do video sessions. After that, I chose to quit that provider and not apply for another one, and then I canceled my subscription to Talkspace.

Apparently the single message response from a provider was enough for Talkspace to charge me $125.

Two weeks later, I received a letter from Talkspace telling me that they had charged me about $125 for the session. Thankfully my insurance covered about $112 of the session, which left me with a $12.80 co-pay. All this because they said I had a session with a therapist. My “session” was literally a therapist telling me that they don’t offer video sessions.

I expect that within the next couple of years, there will be some kind of class action suit against Talkspace. When there is, I will gladly join in.

title: Waste of time
text: They matched me with a therapist who never responded. Then tried to charge me for a session he cancelled.

title: Terrible Service
text: I would not recommend this service at all. The worst experience of my life with a psychologist. Customer service is slow and not getting me anywhere. The psychologist lacked in listening skills, wrote false information on my medical record, tried forcing medication on me, and didn’t make me feel like I was in a safe place. I felt judged, I felt unhappy talking with the provider, and it was just an unpleasant experience. I’ve been in contact with customer service for the past 12 days in regards to the false information on my medical record and I have gotten NOWHERE. Do not trust this company to help you.

title: Dark mode
text: Dark mode would be nice, also I had a therapist that literally typed like he was reading from a step by step guide book. Was not impressed by that, then in couples therapy we were placed with the same therapist, did the same thing then basically took her side saying that the courts will be on her side, not even trying to mediate the situation to potentially find a way to help us communicate properly or suggest that.

title: Poor Messaging Technology
text: I don’t like the messaging system at all. There is no “Unsend” feature if your therapist has not read the message and you change your mind about sending it, AND there is no way to edit a message that has been sent, even if the therapist has not read it yet. These are normal texting features on my phone, and they are also features that TalkSpace’s competitor BetterHelp has — which I think has a better messaging system.  Very disappointing.

title: The Uber of Therapy
text:
The four therapists I’ve been through on the app are, to put it mildly, very low effort.  They don’t read the messages, they copy and paste generic prompts, they try and direct everything from text into a single billable visit, etc.  
I can’t blame them, because I can only imagine the back end of this is a gig economy job.

title: Basically a scam
text: When their software glitched and made me miss my appointment, not only was I without my medication for days, they then charged me for the session that their software made me miss.  Blatantly underhanded. Run, don’t walk to literally anywhere else.

title: Exceptional Online Platform
text: Fantastic online therapy platform that accepts my insurance! I was paired with a phenomenal therapist! SO grateful to have found “my person” right off the bat! Talkspace app is super easy to navigate. Registration was a breeze, and booking & joining a session are easy-peasy. 1-hour live sessions work best for me personally. However, I like knowing I can message my therapist, if needed, in between sessions. Prior to our first session we messaged, and she always responded in a most timely manner. Even during my first session, I felt heard and understood. So far, I’ve had 3 sessions in which I’ve received awesome feedback and support. I have been given very useful tools to help me overcome my barriers to having a happy & fulfilling life. I’m thankful Talkspace is helping me along journey to becoming a better me!

title: Great providers and convenient to use.
text: The app is easy to navigate. Easy to book appointments.

title: Look forward to my next session
text: I have a video session my Therapist was understanding. The video quality was moderate.  Definitely had a few bugs

title: Save your time and $$ and see someone in person
text: You can’t get quality help through a screen. They are limited in what they can prescribe to you as well. My prescription expired and I needed a refill. My therapist/psychiatrist has been unresponsive after I asked for a refill several times. Submitting a support ticket with Talkspace didn’t help either they said they won’t respond for at least 1-3 days. The promise of online therapy is less barriers to help. It’s quite the opposite. Getting in touch with help is HARDER here than it would be with an in-person therapist. I see ZERO advantages to Talkspace. For your own well being, don’t use them/give them your money.

title: Horrible
text: There is no way to contact support. They don’t have a direct line and support tickets are never answered. I am out of medication but I cannot schedule a session with my provider. Do better.

title: I think all the therapist are fake
text: Been waiting two days for a reply when both therapist I was given where both on those days. Also when you try to contact them there’s a a page from 2018 that says we don’t have a number to contact yet. From 2018?!?!? How is my job Amazon working with this company and offering fee therapist we can actually contact? I’m assuming all the therapist for free are fake and y’all hope illpay for one who doesn’t have an AI generated picture

title: Look elsewhere for service
text: It’s been almost a month and I cannot get customer service to assist - going on 3 weeks with no therapy because no one will update my account. My provider can’t even get through. My insurance says I’m covered yet I still cannot book a session. How do I escalate to a supervisor? Or do I have to make a complaints to the Better Business Bureau, Office of Mental Health, ADA, FTC, etc. A month to update my account is ridiculous! I want to recommend the use of this platform but I can’t in good conscious recommend TalkSpace since your customer service is terrible. Only reason I’m still trying is because I genuinely love my provider.

title: Taking advantage/ Totally irresponsible
text:
BEWARE this app will tell you that you’re covered even if you’re not. 

I can all my health insurance threw and was charged anyway (270 for two sessions that were just sending me a copy and paste pdf on what anxiety is and a get to know you session!) I called my provider and then said they do not cover any mental health services until you reach your deductible. 

I should have called them and not believed this stupid app first but then why on earth would it tell me I’m fully covered!? 

Now not only am I anxious and depressed but I don’t get groceries for the next two weeks. 
Totally irresponsible.

title: Waste of time
text: DO NOT use the messaging option as the therapists take over 24hrs to get back to you. You’ll be lucky to even get 3 replies before your message session ends. Even when attempting to schedule a video appointment the app glitches and it starts a messaging session when that is not at all what you confirmed. Therefore a credit is used. You try to contact the technical team and they are no help.

title: First sesh
text: First session went great! Excited for the second!

title: This was a waste of time and money
text: I don’t know if the providers on here just don’t care or if there is something on their end preventing them from providing proper care but this app was such a frustrating experience. Therapists who give short answers like you are a bother or just not responding at all. This could really negatively effect someone’s mental health if they’re in a bad place. Y’all have a lot of work to do.

title: Great alternative to traditional therapy
text: TalkSpace provides an alternative to traditional therapy tactics that are useful and easy to implement in daily practice. I strongly recommend this method to anyone struggling with chronic mental illness.

title: DO NOT USE
text: If I could rate a zero I would. This app states your “estimated” cost after your insurance coverage to be “$0” what they don’t tell you is they don’t actually use your insurance they just default put that as an estimate to get you to book an appointment. Then if you cancel you’re still on the hook for the cost of the appointment even if your insurance doesn’t cover it. So now after being charged three times for a service I never got I’m leaving this review to warn others. Did I mention there is no customer support?? Your message gets sent to who knows where and when you get a response they close the ticket. There are way better reputable apps for mental health this one just adds to the list.

title: Shame on you, Talkspace
text:
The sign up experience is confusing, and even if it is employer provided as a service, you will be charged if you choose the wrong sign up flow (EAP). They will hide behind “no refunds” policy to collect the $500+ they charge you for sending ONE message and then disappearing.

The providers barely respond, and are not helpful with only asking motivational interviewing questions. Mine ended up ghosting me in the process.

title: You deserve better for your mental health
text: Their platform is confusing and misleading. You will get told to book services that end up costing more than you agreed to or were prepared for. It could also get billed to your insurance, and guess what, you insurance won’t cover the premium service they talked you into scheduling. Not to mention the therapy you receive is mostly yes/no questions. No help whatsoever. This style of mental health medical care is absolutely broken.

title: Super late charges and early cancellations
text: They’ll hold off charging my card until over a month later. They also canceled my service 3 weeks before my insurance renewed saying it was invalid yet they still continue to charge me

title: Charges without service!
text: Charged me for a session without having ever received a session or any services! Refused to refund or check message history to see that I never even signed up for a session.

title: Bad! Took $600 from me!
text: Tried to get therapy for my sister. They said that they weren’t qualified for what she needed and said they’d give her another provider - which they never did. She didn’t get ANY therapy and I had to pay full price, which means the therapist she was given was paid for doing 0 work. They didn’t give her therapy but they gave an abuser therapy. I am so mad and disappointed with talkspace. took my money.
Wont let you create a profile without having a card on file, but will not accept any card I’ve input. I tried 3 different ones. Just says “please try again”.

title: Terrible app with bored therapists
text: If you have a problem with anything technical or want a refund your out of luck. They just don’t have customer service. I’ve used this service one during Covid and my psych suggested I go fishing with my bed boys father dying of cancer. The man couldn’t get out of bed let alone go fishing. My next therapist was somehow worse. Don’t waste your money or your time on this quackery

title: Working with Mia
text: It has been so easy to connect with Mia,I am glad that I found her here. I like her casual non clinical approach. I am a mom and a business owner tsp the flexibility really makes it possible for me to get this self care I need.

title: Lol what is this app?
text: All of a sudden I have to PAY to talk to someone? Hm, okay.

title: TalkSpace is perfect for me
text:
Dr Rachelle Smith is perfect for me too. I’m having a hard time coming up with a way to explain why… her voice is soothing. She’s compassionate. She’s understanding. I have Lupus, and I work at Amazon in the warehouse from 6:30pm-5:00am 4 days a week. It is difficult sometimes for me to wake up from exhaustion so I have been late a couple times. She doesn’t lecture me, she will politely fit into the conversation that she has an appointment right after mine. 

TalkSpace allows me to send her a message between our audio sessions. It’s very helpful for me. My mind is not what it used to be. I forget things, and my brain gets foggy, I’m assuming due to Lupus, or because I’m over 50, or both. I know some believe they need to be physically present for their therapy session. For me, TalkSpace is no different than venting to a friend over the phone. 

That said, thank you to whomever thought of this first, the app creator, and huge thank you to Dr Smith.

title: Not Worth the Hassle
text: I’ve been using the app since february 2023 for psychiatric care and while it is affordable (if you’re covered by insurance), everything else about it is a nightmare. At first when I was setting up the app it wasn’t too bad, and the cost after insurance was quite good so I made an appointment with a provider they recommended but after the initial appointment they kept canceling all the appointments I was making with them. Half the time they wouldn’t even show up, and you don’t get a text or anything. It was especially important for me to have this appointment because I’m bipolar and I use their psychiatric care to get my medication. The video interface also isn’t good, super laggy, sometimes the audio doesn’t work or it hangs up without you doing anything. Eventually I switched psychiatrist and the person I have now is very helpful her name is Anita and she’s one of the ONLY providers on that app that actually answers your texts and gets medication to you even without an appointment. But just today after not having too many issues with talkspace for a while, it suddenly decided that my insurance didn’t cover my appointments anymore, saying that the “coverage expired” with no explanation. I also had made an appointment for tomorrow about a month ago and have been waiting for it and again with no warning it was canceled. So after seeing that I started to panic because again this is how I get my medication, it had me fill out all my information again including the insurance information and at first it said it wouldn’t cover it (even tho it did from february to now) but after trying and trying again it FINALLY decided it was going to cover it again but I still didn’t get my appointment back and had to make a new one. For people who want to use this app for psychiatric care PLEASE try to find somewhere else to go, this app is so unpredictable and for people who need medication that can be really stressful. Unfortunately I still have to use this app because it’s the only affordable option in my area but after today I am seriously considering switching because I refuse to give this app anymore money for the care i’m getting, you don’t get consistent appointments, it will randomly decide that your insurance doesn’t cover it anymore, and in general is just not professional. I also want to say that in no way do I blame the therapists and psychiatrists on this app, they are trying to work through an app that makes things difficult for them and their patient. This is my plead to talkspace, PLEASE fix these issues. It seems like many other people are also dealing with these problems and it’s a inconvenience for the patient, for the providers, and a waste of time. Also not to mention completely unprofessional, the company and your provider should be able to answer your texts, emails, calls, etc. especially when it comes to something as personal as therapy and medication. You should be able to put your full trust in this app and trust that you will receive care that fits how much you’re paying and how much time you’re putting in to deal with all these issues that talkspace should be dealing with. If these issues do not get fixed, I am absolutely switching providers it quite literally feels like a waste of money to keep using this app.

title: Scammers
text: I like my talk space therapist- a lot. She is great. But this platform is run by people seeking to take advantage with those of us who want to better our mental health. I’ve been erroneously charged before and sought to remedy the situation and it took months before I could get my issue addressed (you can only email/in app message them and it says to expect a reply within 1-3 days; all the replies I got were let me forward it to someone else- for months!) Then they have changed their messaging sessions from 7 calendar days (5 days of replies) to a word count. Without telling anyone. They didn’t notify me of the change, they didn’t notify my counselor until after the fact either. It’s like that with them. Billing is always pulling some kind ridiculous stunt. Complete rip off. They do not seek to do their clients right at all. Not at all.

title: Lack of continuity and misrepresented service
text:
I was stressed about moving across country and downloaded the app to get three sessions on Talkspace through my employer. I had one live session and then my therapist got promoted to manage other therapists and I had to get rematched to a new provider. This new provider then informed me that she wasn’t licensed in the state I was moving to. So in three sessions I have to restart with three new providers...

This is a terrible user experience caused in large part to Talkspace’s explosive growth as a tech platform rather than a service provider focused first on doing no harm. They make “virtual” sound frictionless, when actually there are licensure requirements and laws they have to follow, but don’t plan for. I feel WORSE having tried to get help and instead getting dropped twice.

title: This online therapy experience is not working for everyone
text:
The therapist that I chose was good but not satisfied. 
It was so hard for me to open up to someone…I’ve been looking for a good therapist for ages but due to my financial situation and lack of insurance I decided to try online emotional support. 
My therapist had a 18 years of experience and all reviews were positive, she seemed like a perfect match for me, but after a shared all my past we didn’t go over any problems and jumped right to my self value and worth when I clearly don’t know what it is and how I can do that. 
Overall, spend $360 on nothing when I could probably go to one real therapy session and get an immediate help. Also, 30 minutes of video call is clearly not enough… felt like we both stressed out to finish conversation faster. It tells you that you can chat with your therapist Monday-Friday but after our 1st phone call she never asked me how I am doing or what I should be focusing on.
I had so many questions for her and none of them were answered. Really upsetting.
Once again, my therapist was really sweet and a really nice person, I really wish it would worked out. Maybe it’s my fault but as a person who’s working with people who had severe traumas they should know that those people are hard to reach out first.

Really hope this app will have at least a week of trial because I feel really bad for spending so much money for nothing.

The only one thing that my therapist recommended me is to read a book called “The body keeps the score” by Bessel Van Der Kolk. So if you’re like me and don’t know where to start from this book will be a great start. Plus, as a nutritionist, highly recommend add to your diet Lithium and Vitamin D, Fish oil (+addition to women “Iodine”, “Iron”) to stop depression symptoms.

Wish you all the best guys ❤️

text:
Included Health has been an exercise in frustration. After more than three and a half months, they still haven’t managed to display accurate basic health insurance information, including claims and demographic data. Our benefit accumulators, including deductibles, simply don’t show up at all.

Basic functionality is broken or missing. The link to request an insurance ID card just dumps you into the Messages section. We tried their provider recommendation service and received exactly one recommendation — a doctor more than two hours away.

And even when the portal is technically working, it’s so bare-bones that it’s barely useful. There’s no meaningful search functionality for claims, no useful prior authorization status screen, and very little that I can’t get more reliably by going directly to my health plan.

I genuinely don’t understand what value Included Health is supposed to provide. It has added another unnecessary layer between us and our health insurance while doing a worse job of presenting the information. Terrible service and completely unnecessary.

title: Dione deserves ten stars!
text:
Hi,
I am spending time to write this review expecting that Dione will get the credit, acknowledgement and praise that she absolutely deserves. 

Had I not used Included Health during the 2024-2025 years, I would have completely lost my mind and gone bananas on some of these insurance companies. My involvement with Dione started in early 2024, when I started getting bills for the birth of my third child. I gave birth 2 weeks before the end of the year, our insurance changed and then my sweet son was put into the NICU (into the 2024 year). I would have never expected the nightmare of bills, miscommunication, runarounds, people not documenting well etc that occurred. It took Dione over a year to get all the bills settled (when I had great insurance all along). I could not have survived without her. 

Fast forward 6 months after my son was born, my other son began having unexplainable grand mal seizures. He was 3 at the time they started happening and again, Dione came to our rescue. MRIs not covered, EEGs that should have been covered for 24-hours but we were constantly billed or double billed. A completely nightmare in the midst of dealing with a newborn and the fear of my other son losing his life to these episodes. 

In a year and a half of feeling unheard and unseen by so many professionals, Dione always redeemed me. She followed up in a timely manner. Kept track of all the bills, their status and what was happening with them. She advocated hard for us and it was more than appreciated. 

Then, my mother died unexpectedly while visiting us. You know when your patience for greedy humans runs out and you wish life wasn’t so complicated? I was there. I was done. Dione wasn’t. She STILL showed up for us to offer compassions and support in an awful time. She took the battles off my plate over and over and over again. The weight of that cannot be put into enough words of gratitude. I’m sure she had so many days she too wanted to ring the necks of people not doing their jobs or not caring about their jobs, but she always handled our case with such grace. She was the light in our very dark tunnel. Her voice was positive and her words always validating. 

For the same person to help us through three very big turning points in our life is unheard of. She doesn’t know us. She could have easily dismissed us, made me feel like my complaints and frustrations were only my own… but she didn’t. She made us feel like she was on our side, doing the right thing and always available to help. 

It’s very hard to find such dedicated employees like her. Extremely hard to find people like her who still find joy and grace in a job that naturally has its frustrations. I applaud Dione to the utmost level and truly could not have survived the last year and a half without her. Whatever had to happen to keep her on my case, THANK YOU. She was phenomenal and someone who represents your organization and department so well. I will forever talk about Included Health to others BECAUSE OF HER. I hope she is given the acknowledgement she deserves. And if ever she wants to leave, I would highly suggest going above and beyond to never lose her. She is a huge asset to your team. 

With great gratitude,
Sarina Barker
