title: You deserve to take care of yourself. Saved my life. Can get therapy in bed when needed.
text:
Short version: 
- You need to take a step to take care of yourself. It’s why you’re reading this review. You deserve to be taken care of.

- You can do therapy in bed

- Not limited to M-F 9-5. Can do weekends, evenings, early mornings, some will even do holidays

- Group therapy options. I joined one session for pet loss after putting my dog down 

- Journal section helps and can be shared or not shared with therapist 

- Mood tracker 

- So many options of therapists
 
- Can shop for therapist based on age, race, gender, specialty, etc, if a similar demographic background is important

- Can easily change therapists without even having to tell your therapist

- They can send you homework to help you help yourself

- Goal setting and tracking 

- So easy to schedule and reschedule 

- Options for video, audio-only, text only, each session 

- I’ve done therapy on my lunch break before, it’s so easy 

This app has saved my life. Literally, it saved my life during my darkest depression. Figuratively, it is saving my life because it’s giving me the skills and therapy I need to build a quality life that’s becoming enjoyable, despite all of the harm that’s occurred. 

I would NEVER do this much for myself if I had to go somewhere to do it. I can literally roll over in bed on my darkest days, and still do therapy. I don’t get anxious about possibly being late and then just cancel, like I would in real life. It’s literally in my hands. 

I love the journal section, and how I can choose whether or not to share with my therapist. It allows us to efficiently tackle things during our 45-min session, because I don’t have to spend so much time telling the therapist what has happened. 

They can share worksheets so I can do homework and build my own skills, allowing me to do my OWN therapy all day, every day, whenever, and my therapist is a supplement to that. I love that my therapists* want me to be self-reliant and empowered rather than dependent upon them. 

*I’ve had three therapists- one, I stopped seeing because I felt “all better”, then went back to throwing myself into work and neglecting myself (despite her excellent advice when she gently called me out and predicted that I was going to do this). When I returned, my second therapist gave me advice that went against my standards, and I was able to immediately switch to my third therapist, whom I adore. I didn’t even have to tell #2 anything, and she couldn’t message me after I said, “switch therapist”, so there was no anxiety over that. 

There are SO many options and you can read about each one, and what they specialize in. 

It’s empowering me to enjoy my life and value myself. I’ve gone from essentially bedridden and unemployed with depression and crippling anxiety, to becoming more self-motivated, understanding myself better, and figuring out what I actually want from my life. It’s helped me gain insight and take personal responsibility and control over the things that I can. 

Life isn’t fair. You’re strong enough to figure out how to get the best out of life using your own talents. This app WILL help you get there.

And by following the course of least resistance towards an online telehealth subscription-based affordable app, I thought that it would represent some form of forward motion towards therapy. What I did not know was that the interview process and the ability of the individual therapist to determine by synopsis whether the client was a good fit or or not, actually yielded a faster partnership than the intervention of insurance stymies. And so, quite without realizing it, I think I found a good therapist for me. And we’re only on our second or third session, but making real progress. Who knew? If you’re like me and you’re critical thought tells you that you’re not gonna find the right therapist for you, give it a try because it’s not a year-long subscription and it’s really about the same price as many health plans copayments, so no harm, no foul, just try it.

title: Pricing structure you need to know before using this service
text:
This is a subscription based service, which means you pay for a monthly service, NOT for sessions. Your sessions will not roll over. If your therapist is on vacation or is sick, the session for that week is lost. You can request a refund or a billing date change to compensate but the pressure is on you to work around BetterHelp’s greedy pricing structure. If you have to cancel a session, that session cannot be rescheduled AND they charge you a cancellation fee. Do you understand now why I say this is greed? 
I’m giving them 2 stars because my therapist was great. I worked with her for 6 months and made a lot of progress. 
However, I strongly recommend you find a credit based pricing structure. This monthly subscription is bad for the consumer, individuals seeking therapy and bad for the underpaid therapists themselves. 
BetterHelp is a publicly traded company so these figures are available to all: they made 1 billion in revenues in 2025, they paid 500 million in advertising and only 250 million in expenses (including what they paid to therapists) 
I’ll leave you with those figures, this is a company that pays their therapists less than 25% of the money they receive. I’ll let you decide if that’s a company you want to support or not.

title: Best therapist I have ever had
text:
I'm 60 years old and I've seen many therapists in my lifetime, but the woman I see every Wednesday night at 7 PM over BetterHelp video chat is nothing short of amazing. It's hard to describe that thing when a therapist is the perfect package: she listens to me, empathizes with me, and I can tell she cares. I feel known. And then she gives me ideas I've never thought of before. I'm sure she's using CBT, DBT, and/or other approaches, but it's not the usual same-old-same-old. It comes from her — her words, her descriptions. When she talks about anything, it doesn't sound like a script; it's stuff she's figured out from her own experience. It's tailored to me, and it's her voice. So genuine.
My last therapist charged $200 for 45-minute sessions, didn't take insurance, and every session she looked at me like I was a sad sack — such sorrowful eyes, her face wincing. Yuck. That was not helpful. I didn't need her pity; it just helped me stay stuck. Did I mention that BetterHelp takes insurance and my sessions are $15?! THANK YOU, BETTERHELP!
And I owe another thanks to the guys from my favorite podcast, Pod Save America — Jon, Jon, Tommy, and Dan. They've talked about BetterHelp many times on the show and have no qualms about saying they use it themselves. One of them said a while back, "Everyone needs a therapist." They're so laid-back, smart, kind, and funny that after one episode, it just felt natural to give it a whirl and sign up for a session. And now here I am, writing this review!
I'm so grateful — thank you, BetterHelp, and thank you, Pod Save America!

They don’t take responsibility for clearly alerting customers when the payment amount changes, and if you miss a session under their subscription you have essentially payed for nothing. The only value of the cost is the human service, as all other benefits are ancillary at best. Your notes app is better than the journal they have. There’s not much in terms of “help” outside of the therapist themselves. Despite the app claiming messaging services, you will be only given replies as the therapist is able. Therefore, you will pay a lot, but benefit only a little. Unless you’re on top of your bill history yourself, you’ll pay far more than expected for these sessions. Refunds aren’t expected according to the company, so it’s luck of the draw if they do it or not. Really wanted this to work. But it seems in person therapy is the way to go unless you accept their rip-off, no notification billing structure.

title: ***I highly recommend BetterHelp***
text:
I’ve felt the need to write a review about BetterHelp since over a year ago. I was hesitant to sign up. I am used to in person sessions, and then after Covid, virtual sessions, which became the norm for me. My other therapist retired, so I looked into BetterHelp. At first, I was concerned about having weekly sessions. Which seemed to be a lot, but now I find myself looking forward to each new week with my therapist. 

Speaking of therapists, the one that I currently have is by far the best therapist I’ve ever had, and I’ve had four different therapists over the course of my life. He is actually a psychologist, and takes his time to formulate answers in responses during the virtual sessions, each of which are very effective responses with tools to help me envision a better future. I’m very fortunate to have found such a great company. If I can’t make a session, they credit you for the following week. 

The platform is extremely simple to use, with text alerts or email alerts about upcoming sessions up until the last minute before the session begins. You can quickly schedule a new appointment for the following three weeks after each session. 

Also, they will work on giving you the best price, so be sure to keep at it with them and they will find a good and fair price for you. 

I hope this helps someone who might be hesitant to start. It’s well worth it.

title: Therapy That Actually Fits Into My Life
text:
I’ve been using BetterHelp for about three weeks now, and my experience has been extremely positive.

One of the things I appreciate most is the convenience and flexibility. I don’t have to get in the car, drive to an office, sit in a waiting room, and then drive home afterward. I can have my therapy session from anywhere I feel comfortable—whether that’s somewhere in my apartment or even stepping aside somewhere private while I’m at work.

I also really appreciate being able to message my therapist between sessions.
